name: Neck liposuction

lead: Neck liposuction removes fat under the chin and along the neck through small incisions to define the neck and jawline. It is sometimes combined with muscle repair.
Evidence comes from surgeon case series, including a 320-case safety report; looksmax.org users describe the results as permanent.

paras: A cannula attached to suction is passed through small incisions, usually under local tumescent anesthesia in published series, to remove fat.
Published risks include infection, contour problems and unfavorable results with poor patient selection. Skin retraction varies by site.

lead: Neck liposuction, also called submental liposuction, removes fat beneath the chin and along the neck through small incisions using suction cannulas. It is performed to reduce a double chin and improve the neck and jawline contour, and is sometimes combined with platysma repair or other lifting techniques [1][2][3][4].

Published evidence consists mostly of surgeon case series and technique papers, including a retrospective analysis of neck liposuction and recontouring [2], a 320-case safety series using tumescent local anesthesia [5], and reports of complications [1][6]. Skin retraction after suction lipectomy has been compared by treatment site in a 500-procedure study [7]. On forums, users describe it as a permanent-fat-removal option for a sharper neck-jaw transition.
infobox: Tumescent local anesthesia in published series

paras: Liposuction as a general technique was developed in the 20th century; the mid-1970s work of the Fischers in Rome and later Illouz, followed by Klein's tumescent anesthesia in the 1980s, are described in encyclopedic sources [8]. Neck-specific papers describe wide undermining with local anesthesia for quick recovery [9], tumescent anesthesia in office settings [5], and ancillary methods [3][10]. A radiofrequency-assisted approach combined with buccal fat excision has been reported for facial slimming [11].

Surgeons note that results depend on skin quality. A study of 500 suction lipectomy procedures compared postoperative skin retraction by site, including cervicofacial regions [7]. The corset platysma repair has been revisited as an addition to address muscle bands that liposuction alone does not address [4].

A review of complications of neck liposuction and submentoplasty states that pitfalls can lead to unfavorable results and that patient selection and correct choice of operation matter [1]. A case report described Mycobacterium fortuitum infection after neck liposuction [6]. General liposuction literature describes risks including bleeding, infection, contour irregularities, numbness and rare serious events [8].

Human data are case series and retrospective reviews, such as 320 cases under tumescent anesthesia [5], a retrospective analysis [2], and a 500-procedure retraction study [7]. Two registered trials, one testing neck liposuction for obstructive sleep apnea (NCT01117974) and one combining ultrasound and liposuction for skin tightening (NCT01735929), are listed as withdrawn [12][13]. A 12-participant study of deep intervention in the submental region for double chin was registered as completed [14].

A looksmax.org thread argues that neck liposuction is a very good surgery for people who do not have a severely recessed jaw and that its results are permanent [15]. Such posts are individual opinions; published studies do not compare it with other options for jaw appearance.

lore.intro: Neck liposuction is discussed on looksmax.org as a hardmaxxing option for defining the neck and jaw [15].

claims.claim: Neck liposuction gives permanent results and suits people who are not 'complete jawlets'.
